# What rsync.ai sends to an LLM

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_llm_egress_doc.py from llm-service/src/egress/, the prompt files and the Go boundary test. Do not edit: change the code, then run `python3 scripts/gen_llm_egress_doc.py`. llm-service/tests/test_llm_egress_doc_is_current.py fails when this page is stale. -->

rsync.ai uses a language model to plan pipelines, answer chat, write Explorer SQL and diagnose failures. This page lists every place it calls one and exactly what each call may carry. It is generated from the code that enforces it.

**The short answer:** names, types and settings -- never a value read from your systems, unless you turn on sample rows. Table, column and connection names, column types, keys, SQL with every literal taken out, statuses, error text with secrets, counts, IP addresses and `host:port` masked (a bare host name is not -- see the text mask below), and what you type in chat. No row, query result, row count, config value or credential. The one exception is [sample rows](#sample-rows), off by default, and set off in the self-host compose and Helm chart: while the install allows them, a platform admin has approved a model and a workspace's owner has turned them on, Ask rsync.ai may send that model up to 5 rows of a table, with personal and secret columns withheld. Every provider gets the same prompt, including a model you host yourself.

## Where the boundary is

- **Only llm-service calls a model.** Go code that names a provider endpoint or imports a provider SDK fails [the boundary test](../../backend-orchestrator/pkg/llmscrub/egress_boundary_test.go).
  It allows no exceptions.
- **Inside llm-service, every call goes through one guard** ([`src/egress/guard.py`](../../llm-service/src/egress/guard.py)). It refuses a caller that is not in the table below, and a prompt that caller does not list.
- **A prompt is rendered by the guard, field by field.** Every variable a prompt reads carries a field class in the prompt file's `llm_fields`. A variable with no class, or a value that does not fit its class, refuses the call before anything is sent. A variable the caller passes but the prompt does not read is dropped.
- **A caller that builds its own messages** is allowed only when its input is not about your systems: rsync.ai's connector registry, public API documentation, a connector name you typed.
- **A tool-using caller sends both.** The guard renders its prompt as the only system message, then appends the conversation: your typed question, the model's own turns, and the results of its tools (the read tools, and connector generation) -- names, ids, types, statuses and scrubbed error text, never row values, except a sample_rows result while [sample rows](#sample-rows) are on. A Gemini tool call goes back with the thought signature Gemini put on it, an opaque token of Google's that is sent to Gemini only, or Google's documented placeholder on a call Gemini did not make. A conversation that carries its own system message is refused.

## Field classes

From [`src/egress/fields.py`](../../llm-service/src/egress/fields.py). Each class bounds what a prompt variable may look like on its way to the model.

| Class | What it lets through |
|---|---|
| `identifier` | Names: pipeline, table, column and field ids. Strings of at most 256 characters with no line break, and lists or maps of them -- also when the caller hands the list or map over as JSON text. |
| `catalog` | Table metadata. Keeps schema, name, alias, primary key and, per column, name, type and the primary-key and nullable flags. Everything else is dropped: row counts, sizes, comments, samples, statistics. A declared type that quotes values -- MySQL `enum('active','banned')`, ClickHouse `Enum8('a' = 1)` -- keeps only the type name. |
| `enum` | A short setting: a string of at most 64 characters, a boolean, or an integer under 1000 (`max_tables`). |
| `user_text` | What the user typed. It is theirs to send. |
| `rsync_text` | Text rsync.ai wrote, such as a validator's message. Passed through the error scrubber, because a message about a query can quote the query, and then through the text mask below. |
| `sql` | SQL with every literal replaced by a placeholder and its comments dropped (`sql_placeholders`). SQL that cannot be read for its dialect is withheld. |
| `model_output` | What a model returned on an earlier turn of the same task. |
| `config_keys` | A configuration map, reduced to its sorted key names. |
| `connections` | Connection records, reduced to id, name and connector type. |
| `evidence` | A pipeline-diagnosis evidence object: free text scrubbed, counts and sizes turned into yes/no, every string through the text mask, then JSON. |

The text mask, for `rsync_text` and evidence strings, after the error scrubber. The scrubber (shared with Go through shared/scrubber_golden.json) takes digit runs of seven or more and IP addresses, which leaves a count written for people -- `7,340,033 rows`, `7.3M`, `12k events`, `4 GiB` -- and a host name. Counts become `[count]`; zero is kept, so `0 rows` still reads as nothing arrived, the one thing a diagnosis needs to know about volume. Bare small numbers (a line number, SQLSTATE `23505`) are not counts and stay. A URL's host, a dotted `host:port` and a dotted host name where error text puts one (`lookup db.example.com`, `dial tcp …`, `host name "…"`, `server at "…"`) become `[host]`. A dotted name anywhere else is kept, because `schema.table` has the same shape and a diagnosis needs table names.

Every class then goes through the guard's secret scrub like the rest of the prompt.

## The checks every request passes

From [`src/egress/stages.py`](../../llm-service/src/egress/stages.py). The fixed checks every outbound LLM request passes, in order.

1. Data markers (src/egress/sample_rows.py): a message the caller marked as holding sample rows is sent only while the install, the workspace and the destination allow them, and only what Presidio finds no personal data in; every marker is removed. A marker the call site does not allow refuses the call.
2. Secret scrub over every piece of text the provider would receive.
3. Size cap: an oversized prompt is refused, never truncated.
4. Added stages (`register_stage`). The public build registers none.
5. Secret scrub and size cap again, over whatever the added stages left.
6. Routing check: the model is the one the caller named, every request parameter is on `ALLOWED_PARAMS`, and no data marker is left.

An added stage may only tighten. It can redact, drop or refuse; the re-run of 2-3 and the checks in 6 undo or refuse anything that loosens. A stage that raises refuses the call: the guard fails closed.

## Sample rows

From [`src/egress/sample_rows.py`](../../llm-service/src/egress/sample_rows.py).

Ask rsync.ai's `sample_rows` tool (api-gateway/internal/assistant/samples.go) reads up to five rows of a table, only on an install that allows them and only while two switches are on: a platform admin approved the model's entry (Admin -> Settings -> AI models), and the workspace owner set `workspaces.llm_data_mode` to `sample_rows`. The install flag, `RSYNC_LLM_SAMPLE_ROWS_ALLOWED`, is unset on cloud and false in the self-host compose and Helm chart; any value but a true one keeps values in. The gateway checks all three before it offers the tool. This stage checks them again before every send, against where the request is actually going, and then:

- a `sample_rows` result must have the fixed shape the gateway builds, or be `{"error": ...}`; anything else is not sent;
- every value goes through Presidio, and a column with any finding is withheld; when Presidio is missing or fails, the result is not sent at all;
- a turn the model wrote after reading values (the gateway marks it) is sent only while the switches are still on for this destination.

Before any of that, the gateway reads at most 3 tables a question, withholds every column whose name looks personal or secret or that a PII scan flagged, cuts each value to 64 characters, never returns a row count, and writes an audit row for every read and every change to either switch. The rsync.ai MCP server has no such tool: an agent token never gets a row value.

The caller marks such a message with the key `rsync_data`; this stage removes the key from every message. A marker on a component whose call site lists no data class, on a user message, or on a tool result that answers no `sample_rows` call refuses the request, and so does a `sample_rows` result without one. Every failure to read the switches counts as off.

Presidio looks for: `PERSON`, `EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `PHONE_NUMBER`, `CREDIT_CARD`, `IBAN_CODE`, `IP_ADDRESS`, `US_SSN`, `US_BANK_NUMBER`, `US_DRIVER_LICENSE`, `US_PASSPORT`, `MEDICAL_LICENSE`, `CRYPTO`, `LOCATION`, `NRP`.

## Every call site

From [`src/egress/call_sites.py`](../../llm-service/src/egress/call_sites.py).

| Caller | Where | Path | What it sends |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assistant.step` | src/gateway/assistant_routes.py: POST /v1/assistant/step (the in-app assistant) | guard renders a prompt, then a tool conversation | The user's typed question, the page they are on (a kind and an id), the model's own earlier turns, and the results of agent gateway tools (the read tools, connector generation, the model tools, pipeline proposals, workflow drafts, lists and branch changes, and each workflow step's type, parents, rule, minutes and the pipeline or model it runs or the chart or dashboard it draws, by id and name, and plan_dashboard's chart sources, their column names and kinds, and each drafted chart's name, type, source and filters, and each dashboard's name, filters, tiles' places and charts' settings (column names, aggregates, sort, the measure's colour token; never a series colour, which names a value, or a text tile's text) and a proposed tile change's chart name, type and size): names, ids, descriptions, types, table and column names, schedules, statuses, timestamps and scrubbed error text, and from generate_sql the connection's id and the tables the SQL uses (the SQL itself goes to the person only), and from get_usage the workspace's plan name, its pipeline and NL→SQL query limits, how many pipelines it has, how many NL→SQL queries it used this month and how many members it has (counts only, never a member's e-mail). With sample rows on (the install allows them, an admin approved the model, the workspace owner turned them on): up to 5 rows of a table, at most 3 tables a question, values cut to 64 characters, with every column whose name, PII scan or a Presidio check at send time marks as personal or secret withheld. |
| `connector_resolver` | src/agents/connector_resolver/agent.py: resolve a typed connector name | own messages | The connector name the user typed, and rsync.ai's own connector registry (names, categories, descriptions) returned by the resolver's tools. |
| `explorer.column_link` | src/agents/explorer/api.py: POST /api/v1/explorer/nl/resolve-columns | guard renders a prompt | The question and the chosen tables' column names and types. |
| `explorer.next_steps` | src/agents/explorer/api.py: POST /api/v1/explorer/nl/next-steps | guard renders a prompt | The question, the query with its literals replaced, and the result's column names. |
| `explorer.query_spec` | src/gateway/main.py: _generate_query_spec, _repair_query_spec | guard renders a prompt | The question, the SQL dialect, table and column names and types, foreign-key relationships, and the model's own earlier answer. |
| `explorer.rank_tables` | src/agents/explorer/rank_tables.py: POST /agents/rank-tables | guard renders a prompt | The user's intent and table and column names. |
| `explorer.sql` | src/gateway/main.py: POST /api/v1/sql/generate (generation and its repairs: the Explorer's with the server's SQL model, Ask rsync.ai's generate_sql with the model the question is answered with) | guard renders a prompt | The question, the SQL dialect, table and column names and types, the join plan, and earlier SQL with every literal replaced by a placeholder. |
| `explorer.table_link` | src/agents/explorer/api.py: POST /api/v1/explorer/nl/resolve-tables | guard renders a prompt | The question and the names, columns and types of up to 30 tables. |
| `gateway.completion` | src/gateway/main.py: POST /v1/completion (chat, HITL and planner prompts from api-gateway and llm-service; the orchestrator healer's failure classification) | guard renders a prompt | The user's chat message, the chat's typed state, connection ids, names and types, connector names, config key names and table names. For the healer: the failed stage, statuses, connector types, yes/no for whether rows were read and written, and scrubbed error text. |
| `gateway.diagnose` | src/gateway/main.py: POST /v1/diagnose/pipeline | guard renders a prompt | A pipeline id and its diagnosis evidence: statuses, stage names, timestamps and scrubbed error text. Counts and sizes arrive as yes/no. |
| `logo_downloader` | src/utils/logo_downloader.py: infer a connector's company domain | own messages | A connector's name and its registry description. |
| `suggestions.transforms` | src/agents/suggestions/service.py: transform suggestions | guard renders a prompt | Column names and types, and the source and destination connector types. |
| `tool_generator.agent` | src/agents/tool_generator/agents/base.py: connector generation | own messages | Public API documentation for the service a connector is being built for, the generated connector code, and its test results against a local mock with dummy credentials. Never a response from the real API. |

## Prompts the guard refuses

These prompt files have no caller, and the guard will not render them: their variables are free text of unknown origin. A new prompt file is on a caller above or on this list before it can ship.

- `prompts/chat/decision_agent.yaml`
- `prompts/tool_generator/generate_connector.yaml`
- `prompts/tool_generator/validate_connector.yaml`
